record.independent_check: Equivalently disintegrate the stopped fine path given each successively observed coarse path; the conditional continuation probabilities give an adapted randomized coarse stopping rule. The conclusion requires strong lumpability, because otherwise the projected fine path is not the Markov chain defined by stationary-flow matching.
record.method: Optimal stationary stopping under Markov-chain lumping structural calculation
record.obstruction: For arbitrary partitions, equality of one-step stationary flows does not identify multi-step path laws. The stopping-time projection argument therefore fails at its first premise. A full comparison needs a different potential-theoretic argument and the later lifting result must be reconciled.
record.result: For a genuinely lumpable partition, the K=1 inequality follows directly. Start the fine chain in any state of a chosen coarse block and use a fine-chain stopping time attaining stationarity. Its projection has the coarse-chain path law. Any extra fine information can be represented by auxiliary conditional randomness in the coarse filtration, so this yields a randomized coarse stopping rule with stationary terminal law and the same expected duration. Taking maxima proves the claim in this special case.
